message: Thanks. To check your options, I need to know whether anyone else lives with you. How many people are in your household, and how many children under 18 live with you?

Thank you. Two more things would settle most of the remaining questions. First, you said you're single, but with seven people in the home, is there another adult who is married to or partnered with someone in the household, and do you file taxes with the other people in your home (for example, as dependents)? Second, does anyone in the household get health insurance through a job?

Thanks. Last question: of the seven people in your home, are all of them people you can claim as dependents on your taxes (for example, your two children and four others who are your relatives or who depend on you), or are some of them not part of your tax return?
Sorry, I need a yes or no to be sure. Will all seven of you be listed on one tax return (you as the filer, with the other six as dependents), or will fewer than seven be on your return?

summary: New Mexico household of 7 (2 children), unmarried, $156k household earnings, no employer health insurance, no reported assets, disability, age or pregnancy info (none reported). Recommended: (1) School meals: New Mexico provides free meals to all public school students regardless of income, so the two children qualify. (2) ACA premium tax credit: at roughly 320% of the federal poverty level for a 7-person household, with no employer coverage, the household likely qualifies for a marketplace subsidy, assuming all seven are on one tax return. Not recommended: SNAP (income above the gross limit for 7), WIC, TANF, SSI (income too high and no age or disability reported), Medicaid and CHIP (income above the children's limit for this household size), EITC (income too high), and the refundable child tax credit (the household's tax liability should absorb the full credit, so no refundable amount). Hand off to a caseworker to confirm the tax-household size, the exact PTC amount and the current child-coverage income limit in New Mexico. The household did not clearly confirm whether all seven are on one tax return.
